newsitem.title: USA: Mexican executed in Texas for 1985 murder.
newsitem.headline: Mexican executed in Texas for 1985 murder.

text.p: A Mexican sentenced to die for the 1985 murder of a Texas man was put to death on Wednesday in the third execution in as many days in the death chamber of the state prison.

Irineo Tristan Montoya, 30, was strapped to a gurney shortly after 6 p.m. CDT (2300 GMT) and injected with a dose of lethal chemicals a few hours after a final appeal to block the execution was rejected by the U.S. Supreme Court.
Tristan was sentenced to die for the November 1985 murder of John Kilheffer, who was stabbed more than 22 times and his body dumped in a grapefruit grove near the Rio Grande.
Arrested two weeks later, Tristan confessed to his involvement in the killing but said another Mexican, Juan Villavicencio, actually killed the American, prosecutors said.

Tristan spent his last day on death row with relatives and his lawyer. He turned down a chance to walk in the prison yard, and ordered a final meal of fish, french fries, jalapenos, carrots and ice cream, a prison spokesman said.

One of 12 Mexicans on Texas' death row, Tristan's death sentence was protested by the Mexican government and stirred deep passions in his home country, where there is no death penalty except in military cases.
